name: Horse-drawn mechanical reaper, Virginia and Maryland
summary: A horse-drawn machine that cut standing grain with a toothed bar moving to and fro, devised separately by Obed Hussey and Cyrus McCormick from 1831.
description: Obed Hussey wheeled out a model of his reaping machine, possibly full-scale, at a farm-implement factory in Baltimore in 1831, and by July of that year Cyrus McCormick had cut a patch of oats with the reaper he built at Walnut Grove farm in Virginia. Both used a toothed sickle bar moving back and forth horizontally. Hussey's machine was patented on the last day of 1833; McCormick applied for his own patent in 1834.

impact.note: Machine reaping spread from these two designs across the grain lands of North America and then other continents (reach 2), removed the hand-harvest labour limit so that grain farming was reorganised around it (depth 2), and began the line of harvesting machines that led to binders and combines (generativity 2); not most of humanity, and one line of work, so no 3.

date.basis: As the cited source gives it.

events.statement: Obed Hussey's reaping machine first appeared in 1831, when he wheeled a model of it, possibly full-scale, out of a room he had borrowed in a farm-implement factory in Baltimore.

evidence.supports: Hussey’s machine had first seen daylight in 1831, when its modest inventor wheeled a model for it (possibly full-scale) out of a room he had borrowed in a farm-implement factory in Baltimore
evidence.locator: Article text, paragraph beginning "Hussey’s machine had first seen daylight"

earliest_record.rationale: The earliest dated evidence found for this capability in this community. No review has yet confirmed that nothing earlier exists.

unresolved.note: The grant date of McCormick's patent: Britannica says only that he took out a patent in 1834; 21 June 1834 is the usual date but was not confirmed on a fetched page.

Hussey's 1831 model in Baltimore rests on this one article; other histories place his Baltimore model and his first field trial (near Cincinnati) in 1832-1833. A second source should settle the year and the date of the first field trial.
Patrick Bell's Scottish reaper of about 1828 is the earlier achievement this card is independent of and deserves its own record; the Gaulish harvesting cart described by Pliny was not researched.

research.note: The Invention & Technology article says Hussey and McCormick were ignorant of each other's work and of that of many others, and that neither had ever seen a Bell machine, a single model of which was imported to the United States in 1835.
